approval_source.question_set: Which injected faults campaign.faults.alerts (injected faults that raised their alert and resolved it after recovery) covers, and where it runs

reason: The launch rehearsals require every injected fault to raise its alert and resolve after recovery, and campaign.faults.alerts had no source. The monitoring drill's stand-in alerting service ran on the sentry's own loopback, so it could not observe a fault that takes the sentry away.

decisions.question: Which injected faults count
decisions.selected: Only faults past a threshold: network partition, host loss, sentry rebuild, validator host
decisions.rule: campaign.faults.alerts covers the network partition, host loss, the sentry rebuild and the validator host recovery.

decisions.question: Where it runs
decisions.rule: Fault alerts are built and observed in the CI staging network only.

unset: Which alert (host and condition) each in-scope fault must raise
Host loss: whether its outage (30 s off, about 35 s to recover in CI) must cross an alert threshold, and how
Network partition: whether a 90 s cut must reliably raise the 60 s consensus halt alert, given the monitor runs once a minute
When the alert must fire and resolve relative to the fault's window (fired within injection to recovery; resolved after the clear or after the recovery reading)
How many repetitions of each fault the KPI needs, and whether CI evidence can count for it on the public page
Whether reinstalling a host's monitor settings is part of the sentry rebuild and validator host recovery procedures
does_not_authorize: any run on a real host
